tb-E101-1.question:
Which of the following statements about a nebula (Fig a) is correct?

(1) It is the birthplace of stars.

(2) It is smaller than a galaxy.

(3) It has a solid structure.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-E101-1.reasoning: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of gas and dust.

tb-E101-2.question:
Which of the following statements about a star cluster (Fig b) is correct?

A A star cluster is a small galaxy.

B A star cluster is an assembly of galaxies.

C There are many star clusters in a nebula.

D A star cluster is formed by stars bound by gravity.
tb-E101-2.reasoning:
A star cluster is a group of stars bound together by gravity, so D is correct.

A galaxy is a much larger system of stars, gas and dust that can contain many star clusters. A cluster is neither a small galaxy nor an assembly of galaxies. A nebula consists mainly of gas and dust.

tb-E101-7.question:
(For Q7–8.) Figure d shows parts of the solar system.

As observed from Saturn, which planet(s) exhibit(s) retrograde motion?

(1) Jupiter

(2) Uranus

(3) Neptune

A (1) only

B (2) and (3) only

C (1), (2) and (3)

D None of them
tb-E101-7.reasoning: All the planets move with different speeds. (A planet with a shorter orbital radius has a higher orbital speed.) Therefore, there are periods of time during which Saturn overtakes another planet (or vice versa), resulting in retrograde motion as observed from Saturn.

tb-E101-8.question:

A (1) only

B (2) and (3) only

C (1), (2) and (3)

D None of them
tb-E101-8.reasoning: Uranus and Neptune do not show new phase (or crescent phase) as observed from Saturn.

tb-E101-15.question:
The Milky Way Galaxy is a spiral galaxy which is about 100 000 to 120 000 light years in diameter.

(a) What is the range of diameter of the main disc of the Milky Way Galaxy in metres? (2 marks)

(b) The Sun is about 27 000 light years from the centre of the Milky Way Galaxy. Calculate the ratio of the orbital radius of the Sun to the average radius of the Milky Way Galaxy. (2 marks)

(c) Name one larger structure and one smaller structure relative to the Milky Way Galaxy. (2 marks)

(d) What unit(s) is/are commonly used to measure the distance/length in each of the structures in (c)? (2 marks)
tb-E101-15.answer:
(a) Convert the diameter from ly to m.

100 000 ly = 100 000 × (9.46 × 1015) m

= 9.46 × 1020 m 1A

120 000 ly = 120 000 × (9.46 × 1015) m

= 1.14 × 1021 m 1A

∴ The range of diameter of the main disc of the Milky Way Galaxy is about
9.46 × 1020 to 1.14 × 1021 metres.

(b) Average radius of the Milky Way Galaxy

= 12×100 000 + 120 0002

= 55 000 ly 1M

Ratio = 27 000 : 55 000

= 27 : 55 1A

(c) Larger: the Local Group 1A

Smaller: the solar system 1A

(Accept other possible answers)

(d) The Local Group: pc or ly 1A

The solar system: AU 1A

tb-E101-18.question:

tb-E101-18.answer:

tb-E101-19.question:
Fomalhaut is the brightest star in the constellation of Piscis Austrinus (Fig k). Light takes about 25 years to travel from the Earth to Fomalhaut.

(a) What is the meaning of one light year? (1 mark)

(b) What is the distance between the Earth and Fomalhaut in kilometres? (2 marks)

(c) A spacecraft can travel at an average speed of 20 km s–1. Find the time required for the spacecraft to reach Fomalhaut from the Earth. Express the time in years. (Take 1 year = 3.16 × 107 s.) (3 marks)

(d) A planet revolves around Fomalhaut at a distance of roughly 120 AU with an orbital period of approximately 1700 Earth years. Find the planet’s average orbital speed in km h−1. (2 marks)
tb-E101-19.answer:
(a) A light year is the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in one year. 1A

(b) Distance

= 25 ly = 25 × (9.46 × 1012) km 1M

= 2.365 × 1014 km

= 2.37 × 1014 km 1A

(c) Time

= (2.365 × 101420) s 1M

= 1.183 × 1013 s

= (1.183 × 10133.16 × 107) years 1M

= 374 000 years 1A

(d) Average orbital speed

= 2πrT = 2π × 120 × (1.50 × 108) 1700 × 365.25 × 24 1M

= 7590 km h−1 1A

tb-E101-21.question:
Figure m shows two photographs of the Sun taken with a modern telescope. In these photographs, there are dark spots on the Sun’s surface. Each spot is designated uniquely by the number next to them as shown.

tb-E101-21.answer:
(a) (i) Sunspots. 1A

Galileo was the first person who discovered sunspots. 1A

(ii) The Suns rotates. 1A

Celestial objects were not as perfect as ancient people believed. 1A
